label: Maria Elena Ruiz, flower seller
blurb: Cempasuchil by the armful, and a bicycle bell you could hear two streets away.

person.name: Maria Elena Ruiz
person.relation: grandmother, sold flowers at the market for thirty years

cards.text: Nana sold cempasuchil at the market for thirty years, and she would not sell a bunch she had not held up to the light first.
She rode a bicycle with a bell she had painted orange, and you could hear it two streets away.
She kept a tin of salt in her apron for the day she would need it, and nobody ever saw the day.
Her hands were always cold, even in August, and she thought it was funny.
Sofia remembers that she sang while she wrapped the flowers, mostly songs off the radio.
Diego remembers that she never made a sound while she wrapped the flowers, because the market was loud enough already.
She made pan de muerto every year and blamed the yeast for whatever went wrong.
On the last night she worked, she wrapped the last bunch in newspaper so it would not bruise and set it on her own step.
